thread.title: UPDATE: While some fret over a trade war, these stocks have been on a hot streak

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: While some fret over a trade war, these stocks have been on a hot streak
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
The prospect of a full-blown trade war, and its potential consequences, and what that could mean for this market, has been rattling and enthralling investors in turn.
But it's been explored up, down and sideways -- to the point where pretty much anything else going on for stocks has gotten short shrift.
That Trump tariff noise did ding a lot of stocks yesterday. But quietly in the background, the Nasdaq Composite managed its fourth-straight rise, to cinch its longest win streak since Feb. 20.
That brings us to our call of the day, from trader Larry Tentarelli, who's all about watching the price and ignoring the noise. The Trend Trading Signals (https://trendtradingsignals.com/) blogger gives us a couple of reasons to pay attention to one particular group of techs: The big money is already there, and new highs are busting out all over.
"There were 140 stocks [Wednesday] with a market cap of $2 billion or greater that made new 52-week highs. Thirty-six of them, or 26%, are in the software industry. This indicates a great amount of institutional interest in the space, with so many names breaking out at once," Tentarelli tells MarketWatch about Wednesday's action.
Electronic Arts (EA) , Microsoft (MSFT) , Salesforce.com (CRM) , Adobe (ADBE) ,Workday (WDAY) , Shopify (SHOP) and Square (SQ) are leaders in that group, he notes.
The iShares North-American Tech Software (https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239771/ishares-north-american-techsoftware-etf) exchange-traded fund (IGV) also busted to a new high, and it's made up of many of those names, Tentarelli also points out.
As for why techs overall are doing better than the rest right now -- the Nasdaq is up 7.2%, versus a 2% gain for the S&P 500 year-to-date -- Tentarelli says tech is "where the earnings are," plus companies in the sector have less debt.
Also hoisting a banner for the sector was StockTwits co-founder Howard Lindzon, who noted on his blog how techs are pretty much inured to those negative headlines and themes.
"U.S. tech companies have been dealing with tariffs -- pirating, theft and a giant Chinese, Russian and North Korean digital wall -- forever," he notes (http://howardlindzon.com/tech-tech-tech-tech-tech/).
Plus, corporations that get tax breaks will "spend that money on enterprise software and acquisitions that we all have the right to profit from, if we position ourselves correctly," he says, noting he's been long business software providers Zendesk (ZEN) , Okta (OKTA) and MuleSoft (MULE) .
Oh, and Intel (INTC) shot past its Y2K bubble high Wednesday (https://stocktwits.com/jdmarkman/message/115356190), while Zillow (ZG) has also been cresting to an all-time high, Lindzon adds.
Time to change up the conversation a little?
Key market gauges
The Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq are moving higher. Asian stocks had a positive session (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-recover-though-worries-remain-post-cohn-2018-03-07). Meanwhile, data showed China exports unexpectedly surged in February (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-exports-surge-despite-trade-tensions-2018-03-08) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-exports-surge-despite-trade-tensions-2018-03-08). (The timing's not great on that data point, given trade tensions (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-promises-justified-and-necessary-response-if-trade-war-breaks-out-2018-03-08).)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-exports-surge-despite-trade-tensions-2018-03-08) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-dragged-down-after-gary-cohns-resignation-2018-03-06)Europe is higher but had pared some gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-for-4th-day-in-a-row-as-ecb-steals-focus-from-us-tariffs-2018-03-08) after the ECB turned more hawkish with its forward guidance. The euro is moving lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/euro-falls-back-as-traders-watch-for-ecbs-qe-hints-2018-03-08), while the dollar is firming up.
Check our live blog of the press conference with ECB Pres. Mario Draghi (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/live-blog-ecb-moves-step-closer-to-ending-qe-2018-03-08)
Oil prices are struggling (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-steady-after-us-output-climb-helps-drive-plunge-2018-03-08) after Wednesday's selloff, and gold is in the red a second day. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-slips-into-the-red-for-second-day-2018-03-08)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-fall-flat-to-start-march-2018-02-28)Check out Market Snapshot (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nasdaq-set-sights-on-5th-win-in-a-row-as-spotlight-stays-on-tariffs-2018-03-08) for more on today's action.
The Quote:
"It could be a deep correction. It could be between 20% to 40%, depending on the valuation." -- That was J.P. Morgan's Daniel Pinto.
The bank's co-president says (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/it-could-be-a-deep-correction-jp-morgan-co-president-warns-of-40-stock-pullback-2018-03-08) markets are about two-to-three years away from the end of the economic cycle. Expect markets to be nervous about anything that relations to inflation or growth.
The chart
To mark International Women's Day, the Economist (https://espresso.economist.com/64fbd809686715480c30159fa7d89d85) is taking a look at the gender gap among the rich. Its chart shows the number of female billionaires in the world, compared with male.
It should come as little surprise to see who's on top:
Here's another one from the World Economic Forum, highlighted in a Bank of America Merrill Lynch note, that shows how many hours of unpaid work women are doing in a day, compared with men. Ahem ...
Check out:The shocking profession with the biggest gender wage gap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/equal-pay-day-the-shocking-profession-with-the-biggest-gender-wage-gap-2017-04-04)
The buzz
Express Scripts (ESRX) is flying after Cigna (CI) said it plans to buy the pharmacy-benefits manager in a $67 billion deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cigna-to-buy-express-scripts-for-67-billion-2018-03-08).
"We don't believe in these tariffs." -- That was JPMorgan Chase chief Jamie Dimon, in comments to Bloomberg Thursday (https://www.bloomberg.com/live/europe).
Spotted: Tesla's (TSLA) new electric semis hitting the road, and making their first cargo deliveries. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teslas-new-electric-semis-make-their-first-cargo-deliveries-2018-03-07)
Former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick has launched an investment fund (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/former-uber-ceo-travis-kalanick-launches-new-investment-fund-2018-03-07) focusing on real estate, e-commerce and emerging tech.
United (UAL) , whose employees recently revolted over a bonus-plan revamp (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/uniteds-reported-plan-to-replace-bonuses-with-lottery-enrages-employees-2018-03-05), will now enforce compassion training.
